how to choose a marketing agency

faq.q: What is the best marketing agency for a small business in the UK?
faq.a: The best one is the best fit: it covers your key channels, shows checkable results for similar businesses, writes down monthly deliverables and keeps accounts in your name. Compare options on those points rather than on size or awards.

faq.q: How much should a small business spend on a marketing agency?
faq.a: Whito's 2026 research suggests £500 to £1,500 a month for businesses turning over up to £500,000, and £1,000 to £2,000 a month as a starting point for meaningful agency work. Productised plans can cost less.

faq.q: How much does a full-service marketing agency cost in the UK?
faq.a: Full-service retainers covering several channels typically cost £3,500 to £16,750 a month in 2026. Single-channel retainers are usually £1,250 to £3,500.

faq.q: Should I sign a 12-month agency contract?
faq.a: Only with a break clause or performance review. A 30-day exit option after an initial period protects you if the work isn't delivering.

faq.q: Who should own my social media and ad accounts?
faq.a: You should. Accounts, domains and analytics should be registered in your business's name, with the agency given access. That way you keep everything if you leave.

faq.q: Can an agency guarantee first place on Google?
faq.a: No. Nobody controls Google's rankings. Treat any guaranteed ranking, traffic or lead number as a red flag.

faq.q: Is a freelancer or an agency better for a small business?
faq.a: A freelancer suits one clear gap and a business owner with time to manage them. An agency or productised plan suits businesses that need several channels working to one plan.
